segments.text: Monopoly was invented to celebrate getting rich. Not really. It was built to protest it.
In {1904,|nineteen oh four,} a woman named Lizzie Magie patented The Landlord's Game, to show how landlords get richer while renters get stuck.
She made two sets of rules. In one, everybody wins when anybody gets richer. In the other, you win by crushing everyone else.
Homemade copies spread through colleges. Quakers even renamed the streets after Atlantic City.
In {1935,|nineteen thirty five,} Parker Brothers bought a version from a man named Charles Darrow, who said he invented it. Then they bought Lizzie's patent for five hundred dollars. No royalties.
Darrow was called the inventor for decades. Lizzie was nearly forgotten, until a {1973|nineteen seventy three} lawsuit over a game called Anti-Monopoly dug up her story.
So Monopoly never taught you to love landlords. It was a warning. Follow for a weird everyday truth daily.
